messages:
sarah: Heads up — support ticket #8203 reporting p99 spike from hosted text-generation region us-west1, started ~08:12 UTC. Customer saw 3x p99 on small prompt sizes. Logging linked: https://support.redwood/8203
mike: I see a correlating deploy at 08:09 from the runtime team (deploy-bot below). Could be kernel/compile flag change.
support-bot: ticket#8203: "API p99 jumped from 180ms -> 540ms, errors 0, just latency" — customer included sample call id: call_0a9c
jade: Is this the flashattention toggle we rolled last night? I flipped a heuristic to prefer FlashAttention for short-seq models.
rohit: Yes that toggle shipped in canary at 02:00 and rolled to prod at 08:08. compile flag SDPA_ENABLE=1 -> 0? I need to check commit.
deploy-bot: deploy/eng-runtime@prod 08:09:14 — sha: a1b2c3d — rolled kernel heuristics toggle to prefer FA for seq<64
lisa: Repro attempt: i ran the same call id against staging and saw p99 ~200ms, but prod is 550ms. Maybe fallback behavior or NV driver mismatch.
sarah: Can someone run a quick compare on kernel selection logs for that call id? We log kernel chosen in trace headers.
rohit: grep from node logs:
```
call=call_0a9c kernel=flash_attn runtime=0.48s seq=32 model=redwood-7b
call=call_0b2d kernel=sdpa runtime=0.18s seq=32 model=redwood-7b
```
So same model but kernel differs between nodes.
mike: That suggests routing inconsistency — some hosts still prefer SDPA or FA depending on kernel availability. Could be compile flags or driver-level perf regression on certain GPUs.
jade: Action plan: 1) rollback heuristic to prefer SDPA for seq<64 (safe). 2) Force canary to 10% with explicit kernel selection for repro. 3) collect flame graphs and nvprof on affected hosts.
sarah: Agreed. Who can flip the flag? rohit?
rohit: I'll push a rollback patch now, will update the config in consul/kvs: "kernel_heuristic_shortseq=sdpa_prefer"
rohit: Pushed, rolling update started.
deploy-bot: config-update/eng-runtime 08:23:02 — kernel_heuristic_shortseq=sdpa_prefer — rollout started
lisa: After rollback, early metrics show p99 dropping to ~220ms on the affected shards. Marking as mitigation successful pending full rollout.
support-bot: ticket#8203 updated: "We rolled back kernel heuristic; please retest and confirm" — cc: @customer
mike: Next: need a root cause. Hypothesis: flash_attn kernel got a micro-regression in handling small batch sizes on cuda 120 driver; or fallback path triggers extra copies when KV cache present.
jade: I'll repro with perf counters on a host that showed the regression. Steps:
```
1) ssh host-34
2) run: ./bench.sh --model redwood-7b --seq 32 --batch 1 --kernel flash_attn --profile
3) capture nvprof + dmesg
```
jade: Also we should add a guard in kernel selector: avoid FA for batch==1 || kv_cache=true until we confirm.
rohit: Filed infra ticket INF-452 for kernel tuning + driver test matrix.
sarah: Great. For support: ask customer to re-run a few calls (we posted new note). I'll keep ticket open until 24h of stable metrics. :thumbsup:
mike: Postmortem step list: collect kernel logs, nvprof traces, driver versions, container image sha, and the specific compile flags used for FA/SDPA builds.
lisa: I'll add traces to the incident board and link to the infra ticket.
rohit: For now, marking severity P2 and switching on alerting for regression spikes tied to kernel toggles.
sarah: Thanks team — good coordination. Keep updates here and paste perf artifacts when available.
